newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - April 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - April 2.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The prospect of making Chittagong Port the gateway to the South Asian sub-region, namely landlocked Nepal and Bhutan and the seven southeastern states of India, may figure prominently at a high-level regional meeting in Kathmandu on Wednesday.

Ruling Awami League leaders on Tuesday said the opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) was out to create a law-and-order situation in an ulterior motive to protect the under-trial killers of independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman.
Some 883 tribals returned home in the Chittagong Hills Tracts on Tuesday from refugee camps in India in the second phase of repatriation.
Representatives of 30 U.S. companies and a Japanese company attended the bidding seminar on Bangladesh's oil and gas exploration held in Houston, Texas, on Monday.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Tuesday told a visiting Chinese Communist Party delegation that Bangladesh was eager for investment from China.
Opposition leader Begum Khaleda Zia said her party would in future hold region-based street protests to match with government steps.
The central bank has asked the commercial banks to demand high margin while opening letters of credit for luxury and consumer items to discourage their imports.
The government on Tuesday approved 23 development projects with an investment outlay of Tk 24.02 billion. REUTER
